text:
Micaela: Ran a 3x end-to-end benchmark this morning on hybrid flash+paged attention, few concerning latency flickers on H100 nodes.
Ryan: Can you paste the run link?
Micaela: https://perf.internal/runs/2387654321
Micaela: TL;DR — seq=2048, bs=8, kernel=auto -> avg token latency ~14ms but intermittent p99 spikes to ~42ms for ~200-600ms windows when KV cache is hot.
Aj: Did it show up on A100 or only H100?
Micaela: Also on A100 but much less frequent. L40S didn't show the same amplitude, maybe different eviction behaviour.
PerfBot: [alert] run=2387654321 anomaly detected: kernel_fallback_pattern=true, affected_gpus=[h100,a100], spike_count=7
Karen: Sounds like the runtime is switching from fused-flash to paged-fallback mid-stream. Could be prefetch window + evictor interacting.
Ryan: Any profiling traces (nvtx/trace)?
Micaela: Yep, captured perf traces and a short nvprof. Key snippet from trace (simplified):
```
[0.00s] fused_flash_attn exec (ok)
[2.13s] kv_prefetch start
[2.15s] fused_flash_attn -> fallback tiled_paged_attn (mempressure)
[2.64s] tiled_paged_attn exec (slower)
[3.20s] evictor run -> reclaim 512MB
[3.21s] fused_flash_attn resumes
```
Aj: That 40-500ms window matches the p99 spike windows. Looks like small memory thrash when prefix cache grows then evictor runs.
Micaela: Re-ran with --kv-prefetch=0.35 and the spike frequency halved, p99 down to ~28ms.
Karen: Interesting. What's the batching heuristic? Could a slightly larger batch push us over the fused kernel mem limit and trigger fallback?
Micaela: Bench cmd: `./bench.sh --gpus=h100,a100,l40s --seq=2048 --bs=8 --kernel=auto --kv-policy=prefetch:0.6 --runs=3`
Ryan: Try increasing batch to 12 and lowering prefetch to 0.3, see if the batching amortizes cost without triggering fallback.
Micaela: Did a micro sweep: seqs [512,1024,1536,2048,4096], bs [4,8,12]. Observations — threshold around seq*bs memory footprint where kernel picks fallback differs by GPU: H100 ~12% lower headroom than A100.
PerfBot: regression_check: recent_commit=abc123 -> changed prefetch cutoff from 0.5 to 0.6
Aj: That commit might be the catalyst; prefetch bump increases transient KV resident size and triggers evictor more often.
Karen: For mitigation: 1) transiently reduce prefetch when seq>1536, 2) prefer batching over prefetch for latency-sensitive routes, 3) tweak evictor cooldown to avoid reclaiming mid-token.
Ryan: Good plan. Can we add a quick guard in kernel selector: if mem_estimate close to limit, prefer fused->degraded but keep a short grace period to avoid flip-flopping? Maybe a hysteresis of 200ms.
Micaela: I'll push a small runtime patch that adds a hysteresis and exposes kv_prefetch_ratio per model route. Also adding a microbench that runs continuous traffic for 60s to catch these mid-run flips.
Aj: If you can attach the flame graph and the small nvprof output I can run bisect locally.
Micaela: attaching snippets below, full traces in the perf link. Flame top shows tiled_paged_attn taking ~3.4x CPU/GPU time during spikes.
```
FusedFlash: 78% baseline
TiledPaged: 3.4x relative when active
Evictor: 2% but coincides with spikes
```
PerfBot: note: schedule bisect job queued (job=perf-bisect-2387654321)
Ryan: Thanks. If bisect pins abc123 we either revert or tune prefetch default and add the hysteresis. Also add QA micro that ensures no >2x p99 regressions for seq>=1536.
Karen: I'll own the QA test and add route-level config knobs to Redwood Console so SREs can adjust prefetch without deploys.
Micaela: Awesome. Next steps: 1) patch with hysteresis (WIP), 2) add microbench and QA (Karen), 3) run bisect and prepare rollback plan if commit is confirmed (Aj/Ryan).
Ryan: ping when bisect finishes.
Micaela: Will do — leaving traces and initial patch in the perf PR: https://git.internal/r/perf/patches/542
Aj: Thx, imma run the bisect locally now.
PerfBot: update: bisect job started, ETA ~18m
Micaela: quick note — this behavior is noisy and short-lived, so many CI runs miss it. The continuous-traffic microbench is the only reliable repro so far.
